content:
maria_support: FYI incoming from CUST-4321 — their rerank results look wrong and the client seems to be sorting incorrectly. They say scores come back as strings and sometimes negative values. Logs attached. Can someone triage? :eyes:

tara_customer: Customer excerpt: "We hit /v1/rerank via your JS SDK and the order of results makes no sense — the top item has score "0.9" but then "0.12" appears above "0.3". Also saw a response once with -0.02 for a candidate. Ticket: CUST-4321-RE-RANK."

maria_support: They included the request/response (redacted):

Request body (as sent by their TS client):
```json
{ "query": "best restaurants near me", "candidates": ["{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"A\"}", "{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"B\"}", "{\"id\":3,\"text\":\"C\"}"], "k": 3 }
```

Response body (server):
```json
{ "scores": ["0.9","0.12","0.3"], "order": [1,2,3] }
```

maria_support: They say their client sorts the candidates by the returned "scores" field client-side, but because scores are strings the sort is lexicographic so "0.9" > "0.3" > "0.12" -> leads to perceived wrong ordering. Also reported a separate case where the python client sent candidates double-encoded leading to 422 validation.

alex_devex: Thanks — which SDK versions?

maria_support: Python 0.3.4, JS 1.2.1 (npm). Reproduced locally with both.

leo_backend: Can you paste the raw HTTP body from the server logs for the python repro?

maria_support: Paste from logs: 

```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
...
{"query":"x","candidates":["{\"id\":42,\"text\":\"Foo\"}"],"k":5}
```

leo_backend: Ah — that's double-encoded candidates (strings containing JSON). Server-side validation expects an array of objects, not strings. The validator coerced some fields and output unhelpful scores; that could explain negative/garbage values.

simon_eng: I dug into the python client. Root cause: our Python SDK was calling json.dumps on candidate dicts when building the body if an element wasn't a str already. For example wrong code: 

```python
# buggy
payload = {
  "query": query,
  "candidates": [json.dumps(c) for c in candidates],
  "k": k
}
```

This produces the double-encoded strings you pasted. The server then tries to parse and ends up in an invalid code path. Patch is to remove json.dumps and pass dicts directly; requests will encode them correctly.

alex_devex: For the JS bug: in 1.2.1 we stringify candidate objects in some pathways too (legacy path). Also we return scores as strings in one response shim layer. Client-side code then does candidates.sort((a,b) => b.score - a.score) but if score is a string JS coerces but edgecases exist (e.g., locales or stray whitespace). We should normalize: ensure server returns numbers and SDK casts Number(score) or uses parseFloat and falls back to 0.0.

alex_devex: Example of lexicographic vs numeric sort: 
```js
['0.9','0.3','0.12'].sort((a,b)=>b-a) // yields ['0.9','0.3','0.12'] if coerced ok, but if left as strings and compared earlier it might behave unexpectedly in some code paths
// safe approach:
candidates.sort((a,b)=> Number(b.score) - Number(a.score))
```

qa_bot: Reg test rerank/integration.test.ts failed on CI: "handles string scores" on job rerank-js-1.2.1. Failure id: 8843.

ben_sre: Also flagging a separate problem: large candidate lists were hitting payload size limits and sometimes returning 413 or partial processing. Customer attempted to send 5k candidates. Recommend SDKs validate and error earlier (client-side) with a clear message and suggest server caps (we have docs that recommend <=100 candidates for rerank). I'll add a policy to return 413 + helpful message if body size > 200KB.

alex_devex: Action items I can take: 1) hotfix python SDK to stop double-dumping candidates and publish 0.3.5, 2) patch JS SDK to coerce scores to numbers and to ensure candidate payloads are objects not strings, publish 1.2.2. I'll open PRs and link here.

simon_eng: I'll add server-side strict validation to return 422 with a clear error for string-encoded candidate entries and add an integration test ensuring the server rejects/returns explanatory error rather than falling into numeric garbage path. Also will add normalization to ensure scores in responses are numeric.

maria_support: I'll update the customer thread summarizing: root cause client double-encoding + JS shim returning string scores, mitigation steps (upgrade SDKs once patches published), workaround (send raw HTTP correct JSON), and note cap for candidates. Will keep them updated and escalate if they see any more weird values.

alex_devex: Draft PRs: https://git.internal/r/devex/python-sdk/pull/789 (fix/dont-dump-candidates) and https://git.internal/r/devex/js-sdk/pull/1011 (fix/score-types). Please review.

maria_support: Thanks team — assigning to @alex_devex for releases, @simon_eng for server tests. I'll post customer update now. :thumbsup:
